title: VII: The Governor’s Hall

teacherSummary.text: Hearing that the magistrates may take Pearl, Hester brings gloves to Governor Bellingham's mansion. In a polished breastplate she sees the letter grotesquely magnified. Pearl, dressed in scarlet, cries for a red rose in the garden.

vocabulary.context: Little Pearl—who was as greatly pleased with the gleaming armor as she had been with the glittering frontispiece of the house—spent some time looking into the polished mirror of the breastplate.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.

hsJunior.note: Emphasize structure and ambiguity; students should name where the text leaves matters open.

hsSenior.note: Weigh competing interpretations; students should defend the stronger reading.
